routes.description: Establish that Paul understood Jesus as an earthly historical person by combining Pauline biographical references with an earthly reading of the crucifixion and historically proximate narrative corroboration.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the relevant Pauline language is best explained by an earthly life, family, and execution, and if Luke-Acts and related narrative evidence can legitimately clarify the historical setting known within Paul's circle.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative evidence must support Paul understanding Jesus as an earthly historical person rather than a figure whose salvific career occurred only in a heavenly realm.

centralBridges.description: Pauline references to ancestry, birth, kinship, teachings, associates, betrayal, death, and burial must provide genuine earthly biographical anchors.
The rulers responsible for the crucifixion in First Corinthians must be identifiable as human authorities, even if demonic forces also participated.
Luke-Acts must be sufficiently connected to Paul and historically reliable for its earthly Jesus narrative to inform the interpretation of Paul's understanding.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The admissible Pauline corpus must not exclude relevant earthly references merely by assuming disputed authorship conclusions.
Incidental correspondences and external corroborations must materially support the historical grounding of Acts and the Gospel traditions.

routes.description: Establish that Paul's authentic letters remain compatible with a mortal-bodied Jesus whose death and resurrection occurred in a heavenly mythic realm, while resisting later narrative evidence as a reliable guide to Paul's understanding.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if Pauline references do not unambiguously locate Jesus's career or death on earth, the crucifying rulers plausibly belong to a celestial framework, and later accounts lack the proximity or independence needed to resolve those ambiguities.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative evidence must leave Paul's Jesus intelligible as a celestial mythic figure rather than requiring an earthly historical career.

centralBridges.description: The accepted Pauline letters must lack an unambiguous earthly location for Jesus's life, death, burial, and resurrection.
The language, motives, and cosmological setting of the crucifying rulers must permit or favor identification with demonic powers.
Luke-Acts and the Gospels must lack sufficient authorship, reliability, or independence to establish what Paul understood about Jesus.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Paul's references to brothers, descent, flesh, and mortal embodiment must remain explicable without identifying a recent earthly biography or biological sibling.
Apparent narrative corroborations must remain explainable through source use, rewriting, literary convention, or selective preservation of authentic details.

sections.title: Pauline corpus and earthly biographical references
sections.rationale: The scope of admissible letters and the force of Paul's references to ancestry, birth, teachings, associates, death, and burial directly govern whether his writings locate Jesus within earthly history.

sections.title: The rulers and the location of the crucifixion
sections.rationale: Whether the rulers in First Corinthians are human authorities, demonic powers, or both is the debate's principal direct clash over the earthly or celestial setting of Jesus's death.

sections.title: James and Pauline family language
sections.rationale: The meaning of brother-of-the-Lord language provides a focused test of whether Paul identifies a biological relative of an earthly Jesus or uses a status term for fellow believers.

sections.title: Luke-Acts authorship, proximity, and historical reliability
sections.rationale: Authorship, travel companionship, chronology, incidental corroboration, and possible source use determine whether Luke-Acts can connect Paul's circle to a thoroughly historical conception of Jesus.

sections.title: Gospel correspondences and literary dependence
sections.rationale: The competing explanations of interlocking Gospel details bear on whether later earthly narratives preserve independent historical events or reflect deliberate reuse and rewriting of earlier sources.
